title: SOC2 cookbook / playbook - personal draft
body:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic personal cookbook for gathering SOC2 evidence and running control walkthroughs. This is my running brain-dump — not canonical. Use as checklist when pairing with Mira or SRE on evidence collection.

High-level goals (what I want from this doc):
- Create a small, repeatable script of steps to collect common artifacts so we don’t scramble during an audit.
- Map obvious risks to who-touch/escalation path + where evidence lives.
- Capture ad-hoc questions to ask external auditor / CISO.

Guiding principles:
- Keep evidence names deterministic (prefix: soc2-evidence_<control>_<YYYYMMDD>_<owner>). Easier to grep.
- Prefer screenshots + short narrative over long logs; auditors love context.
- When in doubt: record a short Loom of the flow.

Control mapping quick wins (draft):
- Access control (logical): requirement -> ensure IAM group mapping + 1-off admin exceptions documented.
  - Risk: stale admin accounts.
  - Owner: infra-oncall@redwood (Hector)
  - Evidence: iam-report-2025-01.csv, soc2-evidence_access_admin_exceptions_20250110_priya.mp4

- Change control / PR approvals:
  - Risk: unauthorized or unreviewed changes to runtime configs (quantization, kernel flags).
  - Owner: platform-eng (Mira)
  - Evidence: MR-412 (see linked_artifacts), deployment audit trail export (deploy-trace-20250111.json) -> highlight reviewer comments + deploy window

- Key management / secrets:
  - Risk: secrets in repo or plaintext backups.
  - Owner: security-infra (TBD)
  - Evidence: kms-usage-report-202412, secrets-scan-snapshot-20250101.txt, notes about HSM integration (where to find certs)

- Data flows to third parties (vendors):
  - Risk: PII leaving controlled environment (low but needs attestation).
  - Owners: product-privacy + legal
  - Evidence: vendor-attestation-docs/vendor-A-2024.pdf, vendor-security-questionnaire-results-2024.xlsx

Daily/weekly micro-tasks (practical checklist):
- [ ] Pull IAM user/group export (admin console) -> save as soc2-evidence_access_YYYYMMDD_owner.csv
- [ ] Export last 30 days of deployment events from console -> prune and annotate (what was rolled out, who approved)
- [ ] Snapshot of RBAC policies for critical services (S3, VPC endpoints, model-store) -> brief note about deviations
- [ ] Check audit log ingestion pipeline health (cloudwatch -> archiver) and export a 3-day sample
- [ ] Quick secrets-scan (local repo) before demos, save results to evidence bucket

Questions I want to take to auditor (draft list):
1) For change control, do they consider automated canary promotion with pre-set gates as "manual approval"? How to present the gates in the trace?
2) Level of granularity for evidence: is a single daily deployment archive acceptable or do they want per-PR level artifacts?
3) For ephemeral infra (spot pods, autoscaled pools), acceptable patterns to demonstrate control ownership?
4) Are shadow accounts (service users created by infra tools) treated same as human users for access review?

Evidence naming conventions (my proposal):
- soc2-evidence_<controltag>_<shortdesc>_<YYYYMMDD>_<initials>
- examples: soc2-evidence_acct-admins_export_20250110_PS.csv, soc2-evidence_change-pr-mr412_20250111_HA.mp4

Where to stash evidence (practical):
- Primary: secure bucket: s3://redwood-soc2-evidence/<year>/<control>/ (read-once archival lifecycle 90d -> glacier)
- Secondary: confluence page with link + short narrative (for reviewer quick-scan)
- If screenshot/loom: upload to secure drive folder and reference the s3 key on confluence page

Notes on interviews / walkthroughs approach (for me):
- Start with the human story: "how does a config change get from developer to GPU node?" Record the actors, tickets, gates.
- Validate with logs after the story: correlate MR -> deploy event -> infra-scale op.
- Bring short list of examples (1 success path, 1 rollback) to show completeness.

Open items / blockers: 
- Need list of current service accounts and mapping to teams (merge from infra inventory) — ask SRE for CSV. JIRA: JIRA-SOC2-78 assigned but needs updates.
- KMS owner unknown (filed slack thread #infra-keys).
- Need sample retention policy snapshot for logs (who owns, where configured).

Mini runbook for a last-minute evidence request from auditor (10–20 min):
1) Identify control ID they want (ask for exact name).
2) Search s3 bucket prefix for control tag. If nothing, search confluence for last export.
3) If still nothing: request a 1-hr ad-hoc export from infra-monitoring (follow template email in snippets below).
4) Record Loom of the query and the export, upload to secure drive, link to confluence.

Templates / snippets (to save time):
- Email to infra-monitoring (subject): [SOC2 Evidence request] export logs for <service> <start> <end>
  Body: Hi team — auditor needs a sample export for <control> covering <dates>. Please run export and store at s3://redwood-soc2-evidence/temp/<requestid>. Include query and raw output. Thanks — Priya.

- Quick observation template for confluence entries:
  - Control tag:
  - Narrative (1–2 lines): what this artifact proves
  - Artifact link (s3 / drive)
  - Owner + contact
  - Date collected

Random brainstorm (for future automation):
- Lambda that snapshots and tags IAM exports daily with control tags; push to evidence bucket.
- Git hook that rejects secrets and emits a small evidence artifact of the rejection for traceability.
- Scheduled job to take deployment traces for any PR merged to main during audit window and put them under control-specific prefix.

Personal next steps (this week):
- Pair with Mira to capture a recorded walkthrough for deployment -> 2025-01-20
- Chase SRE for service account CSV -> ask in standup 2025-01-15
- Draft a confluence index page for evidence with the naming convention and minimal narrative

Random notes / rogue lines I wrote mid-meeting (leave here until cleaned up):
- auditor loves screenshots of policy consoles (less math).
- don’t over-aggregate logs — show causality.
- confirm whether vendor A signed updated SOC2 (they emailed but need doc).

If anyone stumbles on this: feel free to take these bullets and normalize into the team playbook. I deliberately kept it practical and opinionated so we can iterate.

---
Edit history (short):
- 2024-09-12: initial brain-dump after kickoff meeting.
- 2024-11-04: added evidence naming convention and runbook.
- 2025-01-11: updated mapping entries after talking with Mira.
- 2025-01-18: refined checklist, added mini runbook for quick auditor requests.
